test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 02 Dec, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following Articles lays down the duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 47**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 47 of the Indian Constitution lays down the **duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition** and the standard of living of its people and to improve public health.
 
• This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which **are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government**.
 
• While the DPSPs are non-justiciable, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Article 47 specifically emphasizes the state's role in improving public health and nutrition, which is crucial for the overall development and well-being of its citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The DPSPs are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• These principles are borrowed from the Irish Constitution and are aimed at establishing social and economic democracy.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts for their violation.
 
• However, they act as a yardstick in the governance of the country, guiding the state in making policies and laws.
 
 
 
• **Article 44**
 
 
• Article 44 of the Indian Constitution directs the State to endeavor to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.
 
• This implies that the state shall strive to create a common set of laws governing personal matters such as marriage, divorce, and inheritance for all its citizens, irrespective of their religion.
 
 
 
• **Article 45**
 
 
• Article 45 initially provided for free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of fourteen years.
 
• This objective has been achieved with the enactment of the Right to Education Act in 2009.
 
• Subsequently, Article 45 was amended to provide for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years.
 
 
 
• **Article 46**
 
 
• Article 46 directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, especially the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• It also mandates the state to protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.
